headline: Town boards finalized competing recommendations on zoning, trail bridge funding, and golf course irrigation ahead of Special Town Meeting.
synopsis: Southborough boards spent the week solidifying their positions and reports ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting. The Advisory Committee issued negative recommendations on warrant articles concerning two-family zoning, a pedestrian bridge for Peninsula Trail, and golf course irrigation funding, citing cost and density concerns. However, both the Zoning Board of Appeals and Community Preservation Committee voted to advance those respective measures to voters as written. Meanwhile, regional school subcommittees reviewed capital requests and anticipated an 800,000 dollar net reduction in debt service for FY28.

highlights.title: Debate over Peninsula Trail bridge funding request
highlights.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance the full 217,318 dollar funding request to Special Town Meeting, while the Advisory Committee voted against the appropriation due to the project's estimated 5,000 dollar per foot bridge cost.

highlights.title: Conflicting recommendations on two-family dwelling zoning
highlights.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to advance the two-family zoning warrant article as drafted, while the Advisory Committee finalized an unfavorable recommendation over concerns regarding lot sizes and speculative house-flipping.

highlights.title: Support for Parkerville Road water connection
highlights.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Town Meeting approve 240,000 dollars from water retained earnings to extend a water main and connect two homes near the landfill impact area.

highlights.title: Flyers approved for golf course irrigation project
highlights.why: The Golf Committee authorized up to 500 dollars to print informational flyers for its 1.087 million dollar irrigation request, despite the Advisory Committee reiterating that the course should remain self-funding.

highlights.title: Regional school debt reduction and capital requests
highlights.why: Joint regional school subcommittees reviewed 460,000 dollars in FY28 capital needs for Algonquin and noted an upcoming 800,000 dollar drop in regional debt service after 2004 renovation bonds expire.
highlights.body: Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee Operational Budget and Capital Planning Subcommittees

highlights.title: Lift of 2013 conservation enforcement order
highlights.why: The Conservation Commission lifted an enforcement order on 6 Lynbrook Road after verifying that an unpermitted retaining wall on state aqueduct property had been removed.
